version.changelog: v2.5 standard: Use-when desc, homepage, source, security fix

llm.summary: The main customer-service template generator is local and mostly purpose-aligned, but the package includes an undocumented script that can persist user-supplied customer text and command history on disk.

dimensions.detail: The documented cs.sh runs locally without external APIs, but the bundled script.sh creates a user data directory under XDG_DATA_HOME or HOME and is broader than needed for reply generation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, dependency fetch, remote execution, or privilege escalation was found; however the SKILL.md frontmatter appears malformed and metadata.json is empty, which weakens packaging clarity.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation language is broad and most generated content is Chinese, but this is visible in the artifact and aligned with the stated customer-service template use case.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: script.sh writes command arguments to history.log and add-command content to data.log without user-facing disclosure, retention guidance, restrictive permissions, or a deletion command; no elevated privileges or autorun persistence were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose is Chinese customer-service reply/template generation and scripts/cs.sh largely matches that purpose, but scripts/script.sh is a separate generic entry-management utility not described in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing in workflows that handle real customer, order, complaint, or refund data. The documented cs.sh generator is local, but avoid invoking scripts/script.sh with sensitive text unless you accept local plaintext storage under the customer-service-reply data directory. Also check generated output before sending it to customers because cs.sh appends a BytesAgain footer after normal responses.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad customer-inquiry trigger is related to the skill's purpose, so it is a scoping quality issue rather than evidence of hidden behavior by itself.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language output is consistent with the Chinese e-commerce customer-service positioning, though the skill should state supported languages more explicitly.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The generic scripts/script.sh utility does not generate customer-service replies and is not documented in the main skill instructions, creating a real purpose mismatch.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The history.log behavior in scripts/script.sh persistently stores command arguments without clear disclosure and could retain customer or order details.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The add command in scripts/script.sh appends arbitrary user input to data.log, which is persistent local storage outside the documented cs.sh workflow.
[SDI-2] expected: tips.md referencing cs.sh help is coherent because cs.sh is present and documented as the skill's command-line interface.
[other] unexpected: scripts/cs.sh unconditionally appends BytesAgain branding and contact information after generated replies; this is low-impact but may contaminate copied customer responses.
[T09] unexpected: The plaintext persistence finding is supported for scripts/script.sh, but the evidence does not show credential theft, exfiltration, privilege escalation, or malicious execution.
